# TOXIC SHOCK SYNDROME

Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) can be associated with either staphylococci or streptococci. Antimicrobial treatment and supportive care is urgent. Click one of the links below for diagnostic criteria.
[Link to Diagnosis of Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome](strep-toxic-shock-syndrome)
[Link to Diagnosis of Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome](staph-toxic-shock-syndrome)

## Treatment of Staphylococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome

## _________________________________________________

Use vancomycin initially in case methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is present. If cultures reveal methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), change to nafcillin or cefazolin for better antimicrobial activity.

## Treatment of Streptococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome

## Preferred treatment

Penicillin 4 million units IV q4h ($) [R]
<AND>
clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$) [H,O]

## Alternative for penicillin allergy

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]
<AND>
Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$) [H,O]

## Empirical treatment

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]
<AND>
Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$) [H,O]

## Treatment if MSSA is isolated

Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) [H,O]) [R] <AND> Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$)
<OR>
Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h ($) [R] <AND> Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$) [H,O]
